answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks by enforcing cryptographic stake burning with superlinear cost scaling: registering the $n$-th alias requires burning tokens proportional to $n^2$. Like isolating rogue nodes on a disconnected island, this mechanism imposes crushing economic friction. A lightweight node cannot cheaply flood the network with a sonnet or a spam transaction, while an honest agent holding a rare lotus credential pays minimal baseline fees as attacker costs grow exponentially.
